model_claims.text: Evaluating every rotation condition prevents a skipped condition from firing spuriously.
model_claims.source_quote: Evaluate every rotation condition so a skipped one cannot fire spuriously

model_claims.text: When using any() short-circuit, skipped RotationTime conditions are not invoked, leaving their _limit stale and causing a spurious rotation on the next message.
model_claims.source_quote: `any()` over a generator **short-circuits**. That is fine for the return value, but each `RotationTime` condition is *stateful*: it lazily computes `self._limit` on first call and then advances it as a side effect of being invoked (`loguru/_file_sink.py:154-157`, the `while self._limit <= record_time: self._step_forward(...)` catch-up loop).

model_claims.text: Evaluating all rotation conditions ensures each condition’s limit is kept up‑to‑date, avoiding stale limits that cause extra rotations.
model_claims.source_quote:
# Note that the conditions must all be evaluated, even after one of them returned
# True, because "RotationTime" instances keep their limit up-to-date as a side-effect
# of being called. Skipping them would leave a stale limit in the past, causing a
# spurious extra rotation on the next logged message.

model_claims.text: With the bug, two log messages produce three files (an extra spurious rotation); after the fix they produce only two files.
model_claims.source_quote:
before — 3 files (BUG):
  file.2020-01-01_06-00-00_000000.log     'a\n'
  file.2020-01-01_13-00-01_000000.log     'b\n'    <-- spurious extra rotation
  file.log                                'c\n'

after — 2 files (correct):
  file.2020-01-01_06-00-00_000000.log     'a\n'
  file.log                                'b\nc\n'
